Logan / Lauren —

Thanks for taking the call this morning. Attached are BrightShop's consolidated redlines to the MSA and the Order Form focused on output ownership and model training. High-level asks:

- BrightShop requests explicit "Customer Output Ownership" for results generated by customer inputs.
- A narrow training license limited to telemetry/aggregated telemetry for quality improvement, with an opt-out for PII and regulated data.
- No feedback license that permits reuse of customer content to train models that would be used for other customers unless BrightShop provides written consent.

We flagged sections on pages 6, 9, and 12. Please confirm availability next week for a 30-minute redline walk-through.

Elaine —

Thanks for sending these over and for the clear summary. Appreciate the flags; we've started an internal review. Quick answers up front:

- We can agree to a Customer Output Ownership clause for BrightShop-generated outputs tied to customer inputs, with limited service operational uses (e.g., caching, inference) retained by Redwood for delivery only.
- Training: we are open to a telemetry-only, aggregated-quality-improvement license, with an explicit opt-out for datasets containing PII or regulated content. We will need to validate how this interacts with our platform-level safety tooling.
- Feedback license: we understand the ask to prevent reuse across other customers. We typically include a narrow feedback license for model improvement but can propose language that excludes direct reuse of BrightShop customer data unless explicit consent is provided.

Lauren and Karthik from legal/solutions are copied — can you do 30 minutes on Wednesday (Aug 18) at 11:00 PT for a redline walk-through? If that works, I'll circulate a meeting link and a side-by-side with suggested language.

Also attaching a short memo with our initial product constraints and implementation notes for the training opt-out (separate file in Drive).

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Elaine Kim <elaine.kim@brightshop.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines: IP / training carveouts (BrightShop)

Elaine / Logan —

Thanks, Elaine — good, focused redlines. I reviewed the PDF and DOCX. My preliminary legal view and proposed edits below (I'll upload tracked changes to the Drive before the call):

1) Customer Output Ownership
- Proposed: "Redwood hereby grants Customer exclusive ownership of Outputs created solely from Customer Inputs. Redwood retains the right to use Outputs only as necessary to provide the Service (including caching and delivery) and to comply with law."
- Rationale: makes the boundary clear but allows operational uses.

2) Training / Feedback License
- Proposed split: (a) "Telemetry and aggregated usage data may be used by Redwood for model quality improvements, provided that such data is de-identified and aggregated;" (b) "No customer content shall be used to improve or train models for third-party customers without express written consent from the Customer."
- We should add a definition of "De-identified" and a carveout for legal/regulatory subpoenas.

3) Opt-out mechanics and proof
- BrightShop asks for an opt-out for datasets containing PII. Practically, we can implement an opt-out flag per customer tenant that prevents any long-term retention of raw inputs from that tenant. We can provide an SOC/attestation on process, but not per-request cryptographic proof.

4) Transition and rollback
- If BrightShop exercises opt-out, we propose a 30-day implementation window and an agreed rollback/escrow process for any derivative artifacts created before opt-out takes effect.

I will prepare redline suggestions for the MSA sections (IP, Definitions, Feedback License, Data Processing) and the Order Form language to reflect a tiered option: (A) default telemetry-only license; (B) telemetry-only + opt-out; (C) dedicated isolated training (additional fee).

Please let me know if BrightShop prefers different phrasing on the opt-out timeline; otherwise we'll use 30 days.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines: IP / training carveouts (BrightShop)

Elaine / team —

Thanks for the helpful notes. From an enablement/product standpoint:

- We can commit to the per-tenant opt-out flag that prevents retention of raw inputs and excludes BrightShop content from training pipelines. Implementation timeline: 3 weeks to instrument flags + 1 additional week to validate telemetry pipelines and update docs.
- For the "no reuse without consent" clause, can we include a carveout that allows Redwood to use aggregated, de-identified model improvement signals (e.g., token-level loss metrics, top-level latency/error stats) that cannot be reverse-engineered to reconstruct customer content? Wording can be narrowly tailored in the MSA.
- If BrightShop needs dedicated training/exclusive models, we can propose a Dedicated Model Offering (separate SOW + pricing).

Action items:
- Logan: confirm meeting time Wed Aug 18 11:00 PT with BrightShop.
- Lauren: post the tracked redlines to Drive and include the three tiered Order Form options.
- Elaine: please confirm whether BrightShop requires escrow/rollback language for pre-opt-out derivatives.

Happy to jump on the call and map technical constraints to legal language.

Thanks,
